children: Bayer AG (XETR:BAYN) is juggling a $7.25B Roundup settlement and ongoing jury trials and patent suits while expanding with a $2.2B Ohio pharma campus, launching products like MiraSOFT and Lynkuet, appointing Dr. Christoph Koenen as CMO, and seeing Amundi cross a 3% voting threshold.
: Bayer AG (BAYN) seeks to settle about 65,000 Roundup claims via a $7.25 billion class-action deal now awaiting approval from a St. Louis state court judge.
: Bayer (BAYN) to invest $2.2B in a modular pharma campus in New Albany, Ohio. Drug-substance ops due 2031, drug-product 2034. Will support oncology, CV/renal drugs and add ~600 jobs.
: Jury trial opened in Missouri as three plaintiffs accuse Bayer AG’s Monsanto unit of inadequate Roundup testing; claims target alleged design and safety failures. One plaintiff died before trial.
: Delaware judge denied dismissal of Bayer CropScience mRNA patent suits vs. Moderna and Pfizer, letting cases proceed in Delaware; separate suit vs. Johnson & Johnson remains in New Jersey.
: Bayer AG (BAYN) launched MiraSOFT, a docusate sodium stool softener, sold exclusively at 7,000+ CVS stores and online, placed in CVS Digestive Health aisles.
: Amundi crossed the 3% voting-rights threshold in Bayer AG (BAYN) as of Sept 23, 2026, disclosed Sept 28–29, 2026. Announcement covers voting rights per German securities law.
: Bayer AG appointed Dr. Christoph Koenen as Chief Medical Officer. Koenen joined in 2022, led clinical development and operations, and will oversee medical and scientific strategy across Bayer.
: Bayer AG (BAYN) reported that Lynkuet, 60 mg capsules, had previously received FDA approval in October 2025 for the treatment of moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

title: Weekly Recap: Bayer AG Roundup deal and $2.2B New Albany pharma campus
